title: Keith Hounslow's shift to modern jazz
summary: Hounslow came from Western Australia to Melbourne and moved from early Armstrong style to hot modern jazz; modern jazz is small in Australia.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Back to Australia, what about Keith Hounslow's band, how do you pronounce that?

Hounslow, that's right. He was a West Australian who came over to Melbourne purely and simply because jazz was happening in Melbourne. And he came over playing early Armstrong type of stuff. He was playing some beautiful music. He was young, keen. Gradually he changed. He's now playing the most far out modern jazz that anyone is playing in Australia. But he's playing hot modern jazz, which is good. And he's still prepared to have a go at things, even if he makes a mistake or two. He's one of the reasons why I, without knowing anything about modern jazz, I don't sort of laugh at it or discard it at all. Obviously, there are chaps who really believe in it and sincerely try to play in that style. It's a different sort of music to my mind. But that's what happened to Keith.
And is there much modern jazz over there? Is that a big competition? Not very much.
They had that Australian jazz quartet which came to this country. They're not very well known in Australia.
